subject: MedQuant - Dedicated GPU plan, isolation & procurement cadence
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@medquant.ai>, procurement@medquant.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — initial capacity & isolation notes

Thanks again for your time today — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and the proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of pain points you described
- Peak inference latency spikes during end-of-day batch scoring (p95 currently ~420ms) that break downstream SLAs.
- Data isolation requirement for patient-adjacent datasets (must be in a dedicated VPC with customer-managed KMS).
- Bursty training/validation workloads at month-end that should not impact inference SLA.
- Need for predictable unit economics for pricing and a clear path to scale without service interruptions.

Goals you outlined
- Stable online inference with p95 latency <150ms for standard 2k token requests.
- Dedicated pool with tenant isolation and SOC2-compliant controls in onboarding window.
- Pilot in production by mid-August and procurement/PO within ~6 weeks.

Redwood recommendation (high level)
- Start with a dedicated pool equivalent to 4x A100-class GPUs (can be implemented on our Dedicated offering).
- Isolation: VPC peering + dedicated tenant pool + customer KMS wrap.
- Autoscale/burst: reserve 4 units with a 2-unit burst buffer for month-end peaks.
- SLA targets to aim for: 99.9% uptime, p95 latency <150ms (we'll instrument traces to measure).

Open items / asks for MedQuant
1) Procurement contact + PO cadence so finance can prepare pricing options.
2) Basic traffic profile (RPS by hour, average tokens per request, batch jobs per month).
3) Any PO terms/contract redlines to route to our legal team up front.
4) Security questionnaire (we can ingest but would like to align on required evidence).

Attachments sent: MedQuant_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, ~420KB) — includes sizing rationale and ballpark pricing; SLA-draft.docx (editable) — initial SLA language.

Next steps I propose
- Technical deep dive with Marcus (solutions) for architecture and quota sizing — 60 minutes — please propose windows for next week.
- Procurement kickoff: add your procurement contact and preferred PO cadence.
- I’ll drop a HubSpot record and share a Drive folder with design artifacts.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with meeting invites after we confirm windows.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: MedQuant_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf

From: Samantha Liu <samantha@medquant.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@medquant.ai
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — initial capacity & isolation notes

Thanks, Irene — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- The p95 latency target is critical; current infra is shared and we see severe variance. Confirming that "4x A100" is a starting point but you recommend we size up if average token length grows >2k?
- For burst: the month-end jobs are short-lived but can spike CPU/GPU for 6–12 hours. Can the burst capacity be scheduled (we prefer scheduled over purely reactive autoscale)?
- Security: we have a short checklist (attached) with some extra audit requirements (data residency comment + specific KMS key rotation policy). I've attached the internal requirements sheet.

Procurement: looping in our procurement mailbox. Procurement contact is Maria Chen (maria.chen@medquant.ai). She will share preferred contract templates and PO schedule.

Can you also send a ballpark monthly cost range for the start configuration (reserved 4 units + 2-unit burst) so I can flag to finance? A rough range is fine — we need to know if it aligns with our forecast before we commit to a deep technical dive.

Samantha Liu
Head of ML Ops | MedQuant Analytics
samantha@medquant.ai
Attachment: MedQuant_requirements.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Liu <samantha@medquant.ai>, procurement@medquant.ai
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — pricing sketch and next ops steps

Internal note + visibility for the team — copying external thread so MedQuant can see our proposed approach.

Ballpark pricing (order-of-magnitude) for US region, reserved commitment model:
- Reserved 4-unit pool (monthly commit): ~$28k–$36k / month depending on model family and network egress profile.
- Burst buffer (2 additional units, billed as usage during burst): ~$6k–$10k / month variable.
- One-time onboarding (private VPC, KMS integration, runbooks): ~$12k flat (professional services estimate).

Assumptions: 8–12 hour month-end bursts, average request size ~1.8k tokens, traffic steady-state 120–250 reqs/s during business hours. We should confirm with the actual RPS token histogram.

Action items for Redwood
- Prepare a short procurement package (PO-ready sheet + SOW + initial SLA language). Link to HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567
- Schedule technical deep dive (Marcus) — propose Tue/Wed next week morning PT.
- Start legal scope: route SLA-draft.docx to legal for quick review — Ben, can you own the legal touchpoint?

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Related drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleLink
